items.text: Nothing can be hidden forever. A hard lesson for the struggling Name Day to accept as he scrambles across his desk.
The typewriter is still working, and Vila is one step away.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Mr. Name Day? What is that?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: A telegraph and a typewriter. Could this be a telegram from Rayashki?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: But how would they have gotten it out? We never replaced our machine.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: What could that possibly—

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: No, uhm, no, this is actually from ... my brother!

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Of course, I-I don't blame you, but you kind of interrupted a private moment ...
Vila squints, eyes glimmering.
Rusalki have extraordinary physical abilities, including sharp eyesight. Reading the print on the typed letter is as effortless as a glance.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: "Your most loyal yet worst friend,"

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: "Windsong."

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I don't intend to accuse you, but I admit, I am confused.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Is your brother's name really Windsong?

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: It's not like that, Ms. Vila, I'm just ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I know, I know. I'm only teasing. No need for theatrics.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Now, would you let me read it?

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: I ... I don't suggest you to ...

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Oh! Every message or letter the Foundation receives needs to be examined by us. Unfortunately, you can't read it now!

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: This one is still being translated, so I haven't submitted it yet ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: The era of censorship is long gone, sir.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Why so nervous?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: It's only a letter from a friend. How dangerous could it be?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Look, it says, "I wish to hold your hand tightly." Terrifying, isn't it?
Name Day falls silent in sync with the telegraph's staccato rhythm.
The tension in the room thickens with the growing moment of silence.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: If ...

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: If you insist, just go on.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: It is your letter and your right, after all ...

items.speaker: "Windsong"
items.text: I am so happy to hear from you finally!

items.speaker: "Windsong"
items.text: I was so worried that it might be even worse news when I opened the envelope. After all, that's all I have received these days.

items.speaker: "Windsong"
items.text: It took me quite some time to prepare myself and read it through.

items.speaker: "Windsong"
items.text: After that, I sent you this telegram immediately.

items.speaker: "Windsong"
items.text: First, I am so glad to know you and your little warriors are doing well. It really cheers me up after all this bad news.

items.speaker: "Windsong"
items.text: However, I'm still confused by your decision.

items.speaker: "Windsong"
items.text: You're going back to Rayashki! But don't you know?

items.speaker: "Windsong"
items.text: It won't be the town you remembered or the utopia we tried to build.

items.speaker: "Windsong"
items.text: The "Storm" has changed everything.

items.speaker: "Windsong"
items.text: It seems the Foundation has concealed the truth from you, but as your friend, I feel I'm obliged to tell you.

items.speaker: "Windsong"
items.text: As far as I know, the chaos caused by the "Storm" has been around for a long time. Wherever it goes, every building and each person there will be "reversed."

items.speaker: "Windsong"
items.text: By "reversed," I mean they "vanished."

items.speaker: "Windsong"
items.text: I have not visited Rayashki yet, but I've been to many other places it has struck. I saw what comes from the "Storm" with my own eyes.

items.speaker: "Windsong"
items.text: Think about it. Everyone you know may have vanished, and that once-thriving town may only be a ruin now, if anything remains at all.

items.speaker: "Windsong"
items.text: I'm not exaggerating. This is a common fate for places impacted by the "Storm."
The "Storm."
A word she has heard from Name Day, now standing before her with guilt etched into his petrified face.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: So ... this is ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: The truth of the "Storm."

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Isn't it, Mr. Name Day?

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: A-actually, the "Storm" doesn't need to be as serious as Ms. Windsong said in her letter ...

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: S-see? You, Avgust, and other kids are safe and sound in the Foundation.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Not vanished, not reversed ...
His voice gets softer and softer, fading until the next sentence fails to emerge at all.
Despite the ability to transform a thing by speaking a name, he finds no name, no word, suitable for the moment.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: It sounds like things have changed there—changed for the worse. Am I right?
Vila tiptoes and gently taps Name Day on the shoulder.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Changed, yes, but it will likely not be as chaotic and ruined as you might imagine from Ms. Windsong's letter.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Ah, well, I suppose that isn't the point. It's only that, I think you should consider staying here, even after this letter.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Hmm ...
Startled by the sound of miniature contemplation, they turn around and see the least likely person to be here.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: AVGUST?!

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Avgust?

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: When did you ... What are those in your hand?

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Ah.
Avgust raises the envelope in his hand as if holding up a flag.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Look, Vila, so many "eternal souls"!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: You're here for them, right?

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: What are these?
All her unsent letters, piling up at the corner.
Avgust doesn't know what he has found. To him, it's only a trophy, a means to another flight of sea swallows.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Oh, these ones are wearing black dots.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Everything will be alright. We can use these for dotted sea swallows.

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: We can make so many new things!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: Pasono and Nina will be so happy!

items.speaker: Avgust
items.text: I hereby declare that you are all "eternal souls"!

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Avgust ...

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: These are not "eternal souls" ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: It will be fine.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: Avgust is right, Mr. Name Day.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: They could be anything we think they are, including "eternal souls."

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: They're nothing special anymore.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: They aren't going to be of any other use.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: I'm sorry.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: You don't have to. As I said, you have your job to do, and I ...

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I also have mine, even in this situation.

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: *breathes out*

items.speaker: Vila
items.text: I suppose we're lucky you didn't send them. Now the children have some more paper.
